input: FACTS: Directional selection favors one extreme phenotype over others. QUESTION: What is a key outcome of directional selection? CHOICES: A. The population becomes more genetically diverse B. One extreme phenotype replaces all others C. The average trait value shifts to become neutral D. Directional selection itself leads to genetic drift

FACTS: Directional selection favors one extreme phenotype over others. QUESTION: How does directional selection typically affect the distribution of traits within a population? CHOICES: A. It makes the distribution bimodal (peaked at two extremes) B. It favors one extreme phenotype over others C. It has no effect on trait variation if the selection pressure is strong enough D. It tends to increase genetic variation among individuals

FACTS: Directional selection favors one extreme phenotype over others. QUESTION: In a given population undergoing directional selection, which of the following would be most likely? CHOICES: A. The tallest individual in the population becomes shorter over time B. A new mutation occurs that changes the direction of selection entirely C. One extreme body size replaces all other body sizes as dominant D. The average height stays roughly constant due to counterbalancing forces

FACTS: Directional selection shifts the population mean toward one phenotypic extreme. QUESTION: A population of finches is subjected to strong predation pressure, favoring birds with larger beaks. As a result, the population mean shift toward one phenotypic extreme will be: CHOICES: A. larger beak size B. smaller beak size C. unchanged beak size D. more variability in beak size

FACTS: Directional selection shifts the population mean toward one phenotypic extreme. QUESTION: In a small population of pines, natural selection acts on seed length, favoring seeds that are shorter than average. As a result: CHOICES: A. the population mean will shift toward longer seed lengths B. the population mean will remain unchanged C. the population mean will shift toward shorter seed lengths D. the gene pool will become more variable for seed length

FACTS: Directional selection shifts the population mean toward one phenotypic extreme. QUESTION: A species of birds is found in coastal areas, and natural selection acts on beak shape, favoring birds with straighter bills rather than curved ones. As a result: CHOICES: A. the population mean will shift toward longer wings B. the population mean will remain centered around average wing length C. the population mean will shift toward more variable beak shapes D. the population mean will shift toward straighter bill shapes

FACTS: Stabilizing selection favors intermediate phenotypes and acts against extremes. QUESTION: What is the effect of stabilizing selection on extreme phenotypes? CHOICES: A. It favors them and promotes their expression B. It acts against variants with frequencies at or near fixation C. It favors intermediate phenotypes over extremes D. It has no effect on phenotype frequency

FACTS: Stabilizing selection favors intermediate phenotypes and acts against extremes. QUESTION: Under stabilizing selection, which of the following would be more likely to occur? CHOICES: A. A population will evolve towards a point where most individuals are homozygous for a beneficial allele B. Alleles associated with high temperatures will become fixed in a population at high latitudes C. Most individuals will express intermediate phenotypes close to the population mean D. Stabilizing selection will favor populations that are highly variable

FACTS: Stabilizing selection favors intermediate phenotypes and acts against extremes. QUESTION: How does stabilizing selection differ from directional selection? CHOICES: A. It favors extreme alleles, while direction selection acts on mid-ranged values B. It opposes the trend of a directional force C. It favors intermediate phenotypes and acts against extremes D. It increases trait variability in subsequent generations

FACTS: Disruptive selection favors both extremes simultaneously. QUESTION: Which of the following is a characteristic of disruptive selection? CHOICES: A. Favors intermediate phenotypes over extremes B. Leads to increased variation in a population C. Favors both extreme phenotypes simultaneously D. Results in a uniform gene pool in a population

FACTS: Disruptive selection favors both extremes simultaneously. QUESTION: In a study on the size of birds' beaks, which result would you expect if disruptive selection was occurring? CHOICES: A. Most birds have large or small beaks with intermediate sizes being rare B. Most birds have medium-sized beaks only C. Beak size has no effect on bird survival and reproduction D. Individuals with very few feathers are more likely to survive

FACTS: Disruptive selection favors both extremes simultaneously. QUESTION: Disruptive selection typically occurs in populations where there is: CHOICES: A. Excessive genetic variation, preventing natural selection from acting effectively B. Strong competition among individuals for limited resources C. Genetic diversity that leads some individuals to be adapted to specific environmental pressures D. All individuals having similar adaptations and traits

FACTS: Sexual selection occurs through mate choice and competition for mates. QUESTION: What drives the evolution of exaggerated traits in some animal species? CHOICES: A. Habitat specialization B. Mate choice and competition for mates, as seen in sexual selection C. Genetic drift and mutation only D. Disease resistance and adaptation to climate change

FACTS: Sexual selection occurs through mate choice and competition for mates. QUESTION: In what way does mate choice contribute to sexual selection? CHOICES: A. Only through physical interaction between individuals B. Mainly through social hierarchy and dominance C. By selectively choosing mates based on desirable traits, increasing the likelihood of genetic diversity and advantageous characteristics passing on D. Through competition for food resources only

FACTS: Sexual selection occurs through mate choice and competition for mates. QUESTION: Which process results in species exhibiting adaptations that improve mating success? CHOICES: A. Natural selection favoring traits related to survival rather than reproduction B. Genetic drift due to random events C. The combination of mate preference and competition between potential mates driving the evolution of specialized traits for reproduction D. Convergent evolution, where different species develop similar traits in response to environmental pressures

FACTS: Natural selection requires that some individuals reproduce more than others. QUESTION: What is necessary for natural selection to occur? CHOICES: A. All individuals in a population must reproduce an equal number of offspring. B. Some individuals in a population must produce more offspring than others. C. The environment does not have any impact on individual reproduction. D. No individuals in a population can or will ever reproduce.

FACTS: Natural selection requires that some individuals reproduce more than others. QUESTION: Which of the following best describes the role of variation in populations under natural selection? CHOICES: A. Variation leads to identical traits among all individuals, promoting equality. B. Variation allows for some individuals to have more offspring than others, giving an edge in reproduction. C. Variation causes populations to become extinct due to lack of cohesion. D. Variation is irrelevant and has no effect on population dynamics.

FACTS: Natural selection requires that some individuals reproduce more than others. QUESTION: If all individuals in a population reproduced with equal success, what would likely happen? CHOICES: A. Natural selection would cause the population's average fitness to increase over time. B. The genetic makeup of the population would remain largely unchanged over generations. C. The rate of adaptation and evolution of the population would decrease significantly. D. All traits in the population would become identical.

FACTS: Genetic drift has a larger effect on small populations. QUESTION: What effect does genetic drift have on populations of different sizes? CHOICES: A. It has no effect, regardless of population size. B. It is more pronounced in large populations. C. It has a larger effect on small populations. D. It doesn't occur at all in large ecosystems.

FACTS: Genetic drift has a larger effect on small populations. QUESTION: Which group would be most affected by genetic drift? CHOICES: A. A large city with millions of people B. A colony of rabbits in the forest C. All human populations equally D. A big corporation with employees from diverse backgrounds

FACTS: Genetic drift has a larger effect on small populations. QUESTION: What is the likely outcome when genetic drift occurs in small animal groups? CHOICES: A. Their diversity will significantly increase. B. They will exhibit extreme adaptations to their environment. C. Their population size will rapidly decrease. D. They become more homogeneous, losing genetic variation.

FACTS: Genetic drift causes random changes in allele frequency unrelated to fitness. QUESTION: What is a primary consequence of genetic drift in populations? CHOICES: A. A gradual increase in allele frequency due to natural selection. B. A random change in allele frequency unrelated to fitness. C. The disappearance of alleles with low frequencies. D. The formation of new species through speciation.

FACTS: Genetic drift causes random changes in allele frequency unrelated to fitness. QUESTION: Which of the following best describes genetic drift? CHOICES: A. A process where only the fittest individuals are more likely to reproduce. B. A phenomenon that causes population sizes to adapt to their environment. C. A random change in allele frequency unrelated to fitness. D. A natural process driven by climate and environmental factors.

FACTS: Genetic drift causes random changes in allele frequency unrelated to fitness. QUESTION: Why does genetic drift not necessarily lead to a reduction in population fitness? CHOICES: A. Because it only happens when mutation rates are high. B. Because it is accompanied by other mechanisms such as gene flow. C. Because it causes random changes in allele frequency unrelated to fitness. D. Because natural selection can compensate for its effects.

FACTS: Gene flow occurs when individuals migrate and introduce new alleles. QUESTION: What happens to an allele when gene flow occurs in a population? CHOICES: A. It is eliminated from the population. B. It becomes fixed, meaning all individuals have it. C. It is introduced and added to the existing alleles. D. It mutates into a new trait.

FACTS: Gene flow occurs when individuals migrate and introduce new alleles. QUESTION: Gene flow can result in an increase in genetic variation within a population if... CHOICES: A. All individuals migrate together as a group. B. Only genetically identical individuals move between populations. C. Individuals from one population introduce new alleles to another population. D. A large number of mutations occur suddenly.

FACTS: Gene flow occurs when individuals migrate and introduce new alleles. QUESTION: Which statement best describes gene flow? CHOICES: A. The movement of genetic material from parent to offspring without recombination. B. The exchange of genetic information between closely related organisms. C. The introduction of new alleles to a population through individual migration. D. A mechanism for increasing genetic diversity due to reduced mutation rates.

FACTS: The founder effect occurs when a small group establishes a new population. QUESTION: What typically happens to a group's genetic diversity when it undergoes the founder effect? CHOICES: A. It increases significantly due to the influx of new individuals B. It remains constant, unaffected by the small population size C. It decreases because random chance eliminates many genetic variants D. It is completely determined by the surrounding environment

FACTS: The founder effect occurs when a small group establishes a new population. QUESTION: Which of the following populations would be most vulnerable to the founder effect? CHOICES: A. A large colony with hundreds of thousands of individuals B. A group of 10 animals that migrate to a new island C. A species-wide migration to a new continent D. An isolated cluster of 5,000 plants

FACTS: The founder effect occurs when a small group establishes a new population. QUESTION: What is one of the primary consequences of the founder effect on the resulting population? CHOICES: A. It will have more genetic traits from its original ancestral group. B. It will be better adapted to the local climate and predators. C. Its members may not exhibit the same physical characteristics. D. All individuals will display exactly the same features due to identical genetic makeup.

FACTS: A population bottleneck drastically reduces genetic diversity. QUESTION: What is one effect of a population bottleneck? CHOICES: A. Increased genetic diversity B. Dramatic increase in population size C. A drastic reduction in gene flow between populations D. A shift in the species' habitat preference

FACTS: A population bottleneck drastically reduces genetic diversity. QUESTION: Which event is likely to result from a population bottleneck? CHOICES: A. The introduction of new alleles into a population B. An adaptive radiation event as populations radiate outwards C. A drastic reduction in genetic diversity D. A decrease in the rate of natural selection acting on the population

FACTS: A population bottleneck drastically reduces genetic diversity. QUESTION: How is a bottleneck event typically viewed by biologists? CHOICES: A. As a minor disruption to gene flow with little long-term impact B. As an opportunity for evolutionary innovation and adaptation C. As a major reduction in genetic diversity that often affects future generations D. As an example of speciation occurring rapidly

FACTS: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium assumes no selection, drift, mutation, migration, or non-random mating. QUESTION: What is one of the key assumptions made by the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium model? CHOICES: A. Random mutation events occur with equal frequency in each generation. B. None of the above assumptions impact the dynamics of allele frequencies at a particular locus. C. The population size remains constant across multiple generations with no migration. D. Populations are allowed to interbreed randomly without restriction.

FACTS: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium assumes no selection, drift, mutation, migration, or non-random mating. QUESTION: Which of the following factors would affect the equilibrium predicted by the Hardy-Weinberg model? CHOICES: A. Natural selection against recessive alleles B. Genetic mutation rates causing changes in allele frequencies C. Non-random mating resulting from cultural preferences D. All of the above options are assumed away in order to derive the Hardy-Weinberg equation.

FACTS: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium assumes no selection, drift, mutation, migration, or non-random mating. QUESTION: According to the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, what assumption is made about population movement? CHOICES: A. Genetically similar populations on neighboring islands exchange a few individuals. B. The gene pool is affected by the influx of new alleles from external sources. C. No individual ever migrates between populations. D. Gene flow occurs, but at extremely low frequencies.

FACTS: Divergent evolution produces different structures from a common ancestor. QUESTION: What is a primary outcome of divergent evolution? CHOICES: A. Convergent structures among unrelated species B. Reduction in genetic variation over time C. Development of identical traits in different organisms D. Formation of distinct structures from a common ancestor

FACTS: Divergent evolution produces different structures from a common ancestor. QUESTION: How do species that undergo divergent evolution differ from each other? CHOICES: A. They retain identical physical features. B. They exhibit the same level of genetic diversity. C. They exhibit similar behavioral patterns. D. They develop unique structures due to shared ancestry.

FACTS: Divergent evolution produces different structures from a common ancestor. QUESTION: What is a fundamental characteristic of organisms resulting from divergent evolution? CHOICES: A. Uniform growth rates across all species B. Gradual changes in morphological features over time C. Complete absence of common characteristics D. Different structures formed from an identical set of genetic instructions

FACTS: Homologous structures are inherited from a shared ancestor. QUESTION: What is a primary characteristic of homologous structures? CHOICES: A. They are similar in terms of function only B. They share a common origin from a shared ancestor C. They develop independently of each other D. They show no similarity in form or structure between species

FACTS: Homologous structures are inherited from a shared ancestor. QUESTION: How do homologous limbs support evolution? CHOICES: A. By showing that all organisms are unrelated B. By demonstrating parallel evolution C. By indicating that they share a common lineage from a shared ancestor D. By illustrating the principle of recapitulation theory

FACTS: Homologous structures are inherited from a shared ancestor. QUESTION: What can comparing homologous structures reveal about an organism's evolutionary history? CHOICES: A. Its entire family tree, including all ancestors and descendants B. A direct correlation between structure and function C. Shared ancestry with other species due to inheritance from a common ancestor D. Information about the species' diet or habitat preference

FACTS: Analogous structures evolved independently in different lineages. QUESTION: What does it mean when two structures in different organisms have similar functions but developed from distinct embryonic tissues? CHOICES: A. Heterochrony B. Analogous structures evolved independently in different lineages. C. Homology D. Convergent evolution is not happening.

FACTS: Analogous structures evolved independently in different lineages. QUESTION: Birds' wings and insects' wings are examples of which phenomenon, where unrelated lineages develop similar traits over time? CHOICES: A. Vestigial structures B. Synapomorphies C. Analogous structures evolved independently in different lineages. D. Embryonic similarity

FACTS: Analogous structures evolved independently in different lineages. QUESTION: This is an example of analogous structures evolving independently in different lineages, where two unrelated organisms develop a similar trait by separate means. CHOICES: A. Homoplasy B. Convergent evolution C. Analogous structures evolved independently in different lineages. D. Parallelism

FACTS: Adaptive radiation produces many new species filling available niches. QUESTION: What is one result of adaptive radiation in an ecosystem? CHOICES: A. A single species becomes dominant and drives out all others. B. Many new species fill available niches, increasing competition for resources. C. One species evolves into a completely different taxonomic group. D. New species are formed through the hybridization of two parental species.

FACTS: Adaptive radiation produces many new species filling available niches. QUESTION: What is happening to species diversity in an ecosystem that undergoes adaptive radiation? CHOICES: A. It remains static due to limited environmental pressures. B. It decreases as dominant species outcompete and displace others. C. Species populations often decline or go extinct, leading to a decrease in total species numbers. D. Multiple new species are formed through the adaptation of existing genera.

FACTS: Adaptive radiation produces many new species filling available niches. QUESTION: What is one key consequence of adaptive radiation producing many new species? CHOICES: A. Ecological niches become increasingly monopolized by a smaller number of dominant species. B. The process creates isolated, endemic populations with limited opportunities for gene flow and genetic exchange between them. C. It leads to an increase in species diversity as many different niches are occupied. D. A population's ability to adapt to changing environmental pressures is severely reduced.

FACTS: Speciation requires reproductive isolation between populations. QUESTION: What is the primary mechanism for the formation of new species? CHOICES: A. Mutation and natural selection B. Gene flow and genetic drift C. Reproductive isolation between populations D. Geographic barriers and time

FACTS: Speciation requires reproductive isolation between populations. QUESTION: Why does a population that is geographically isolated from its sister taxon eventually become a distinct species? CHOICES: A. Because of adaptations to different environments B. Because of gene flow that increases genetic similarity C. Because reproductive isolation prevents interbreeding D. Because the two populations share common ancestors

FACTS: Speciation requires reproductive isolation between populations. QUESTION: What would happen if a population was not reproductively isolated from its sister taxon? CHOICES: A. Speciation would occur immediately B. The two populations would eventually become distinct species C. Genetic variation would increase, but speciation would still require external factors D. Speciation would not be possible

FACTS: Allopatric speciation occurs when populations are geographically separated. QUESTION: What is a major factor leading to allopatric speciation? CHOICES: A. Changes in local climate B. Mutations causing physical differences within populations C. Geographical separation of populations D. Random genetic drift

FACTS: Allopatric speciation occurs when populations are geographically separated. QUESTION: Which of the following scenarios would be an example of allopatric speciation? CHOICES: A. A group of rabbits migrates to a new island where they encounter a similar species. B. A population of finches splits into two groups, one on each side of a river. C. Two species of birds diverge in their preference for nesting materials D. A single pair of bees begins to produce offspring after a long period of isolation

FACTS: Allopatric speciation occurs when populations are geographically separated. QUESTION: Why does the geographical separation necessary for allopatric speciation prevent gene flow between populations? CHOICES: A. Because they live at very different elevations. B. Because one population is in a state of dormancy during winter months C. Due to physical barriers such as mountains or oceans separating them D. Because they follow a unique mating schedule based on moon cycles

FACTS: Sympatric speciation occurs without geographic separation. QUESTION: What is a defining characteristic of sympatric speciation? CHOICES: A. Geographic isolation between two populations B. Adaptation to different ecosystems within the same geographic range C. Speciation that occurs without geographic separation D. Sympatric speciation is only visible under a microscope

FACTS: Sympatric speciation occurs without geographic separation. QUESTION: How does sympatric speciation differ from other modes of speciation? CHOICES: A. It requires significant genetic similarity between populations B. It happens in areas with limited geographical features C. It occurs without geographic separation, unlike allopatric speciation D. It results in the formation of multiple species at once

FACTS: Sympatric speciation occurs without geographic separation. QUESTION: What condition is necessary for sympatric speciation to occur? CHOICES: A. The presence of predators that favor genetic variation B. Geographic isolation between populations C. Competition with other organisms for a limited resource D. A steady food supply without predators or competitors

FACTS: Mitochondria produce ATP through oxidative phosphorylation. QUESTION: What is the primary function of mitochondria in terms of energy production? CHOICES: A. To synthesize amino acids from glucose B. To convert fatty acids into triglycerides C. To produce ATP through oxidative phosphorylation D. To produce NADH from NAD+ and oxygen

FACTS: Mitochondria produce ATP through oxidative phosphorylation. QUESTION: Which biological process is used by mitochondria to generate energy in cells? CHOICES: A. Fermentation B. Photosynthesis C. Respiration D. Osmosis

FACTS: Mitochondria produce ATP through oxidative phosphorylation. QUESTION: What occurs within the mitochondria when the cell needs more ATP during times of high activity? CHOICES: A. The production of glycolysis is upregulated B. The electron transport chain becomes less efficient C. Oxidative phosphorylation takes place to produce ATP D. Lysosomes synthesize ATP using ATPase enzymes

FACTS: Mitochondria have their own circular DNA inherited maternally. QUESTION: Which of the following is true about the DNA found in mitochondria? CHOICES: A. It is a linear molecule and is inherited paternally. B. It is a circular molecule and is inherited maternally. C. It is identical to the DNA found in the cell's nucleus. D. It is primarily composed of RNA.

FACTS: Mitochondria have their own circular DNA inherited maternally. QUESTION: Who is responsible for passing on mitochondrial DNA from one generation to the next? CHOICES: A. The mother only B. The father only C. Both parents equally D. Only through horizontal gene transfer

FACTS: Mitochondria have their own circular DNA inherited maternally. QUESTION: What distinguishes the DNA found in mitochondria from regular nuclear DNA? CHOICES: A. Its double helix structure B. Its linear shape C. It is inherited maternally D. Its high codon usage bias

FACTS: Chloroplasts convert light energy into glucose through photosynthesis. QUESTION: What is the primary role of chloroplasts in plant cells? CHOICES: A. To store glucose B. To regulate water balance C. To convert light energy into glucose through photosynthesis D. To synthesize proteins

FACTS: Chloroplasts convert light energy into glucose through photosynthesis. QUESTION: How do chloroplasts, on a molecular level, produce the energy needed for plants to grow? CHOICES: A. Through cellular respiration B. By converting oxygen into carbon dioxide C. Through the process of photosynthesis, using light energy to synthesise glucose D. By breaking down starch into simpler sugars

FACTS: Chloroplasts convert light energy into glucose through photosynthesis. QUESTION: Why is photosynthesis an essential process in plant life? CHOICES: A. It allows plants to respond quickly to environmental changes. B. It helps regulate blood pressure in humans and other animals C. Chloroplasts convert light energy into glucose through photosynthesis, which provides the energy and organic compounds required by plants for growth. D. It enables plants to migrate to new habitats
FACTS: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll that absorbs light energy. QUESTION: What is contained in chloroplasts? CHOICES: A. DNA B. Chlorophyll C. Protein enzymes D. Fatty acids

FACTS: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll that absorbs light energy. QUESTION: What role does chlorophyll play in chloroplasts? CHOICES: A. It produces energy through chemical reactions B. It helps store genetic information for the plant C. It absorbs light energy from the sun D. It facilitates the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide

FACTS: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll that absorbs light energy. QUESTION: Why do plants need chloroplasts? CHOICES: A. To regulate their temperature B. To contain DNA C. Because they need a compartment to store water D. To contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light energy for photosynthesis

FACTS: The ER synthesizes proteins (rough ER) and lipids (smooth ER). QUESTION: What role does the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) play in protein synthesis? CHOICES: A. It helps to recycle waste materials in the cell. B. It synthesizes proteins and lipids, but not carbohydrates. C. It is responsible for transporting proteins out of the nucleus. D. It synthesizes proteins and lipids as needed by the cell.

FACTS: The ER synthesizes proteins (rough ER) and lipids (smooth ER). QUESTION: What type of endoplasmic reticulum is involved in the synthesis of lipids? CHOICES: A. Ribosome-studded ER B. Smooth ER C. Golgi apparatus ER D. Microtubule-associated ER

FACTS: The ER synthesizes proteins (rough ER) and lipids (smooth ER). QUESTION: Where are proteins and lipids typically made within the cell based on this fact? CHOICES: A. Only in the nucleus. B. Largely in the mitochondria, with occasional synthesis in the chloroplasts. C. In both the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) and smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER). D. Only in the lysosomes.

FACTS: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins. QUESTION: What is a primary function of the Golgi apparatus in eukaryotic cells? CHOICES: A. To synthesize proteins from scratch B. To modify, sort, and package proteins for transport to other parts of the cell or secretion C. To recycle broken-down cellular organelles and debris D. To regulate gene expression by transcribing DNA into RNA

FACTS: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins. QUESTION: Which of the following best describes the role of the Golgi apparatus in protein processing? CHOICES: A. It creates and activates proteins for immediate use in cellular processes. B. It packages newly synthesized proteins for transport to other parts of the cell or secretion. C. It synthesizes new nucleic acids from scratch using external nutrients. D. It decodes mRNA signals for transcription regulation.

FACTS: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins. QUESTION: What process does the Golgi apparatus help facilitate by modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins? CHOICES: A. Translation B. Transcription C. Protein degradation and recycling through autophagy D. Transporting molecules across the cell membrane via various channels or receptors

FACTS: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down cellular waste. QUESTION: What is the primary function of lysosomes in a cell? CHOICES: A. To synthesize new proteins B. To transmit signals across the cell membrane C. To break down cellular waste and recycle cellular components D. To provide structural support to the cell

FACTS: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down cellular waste. QUESTION: Which of the following enzymes would not be found in lysosomes? CHOICES: A. Proteases B. Lactase C. Catalase D. Peptidases

FACTS: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down cellular waste. QUESTION: What happens to cellular waste once it is engulfed by a lysosome? CHOICES: A. It is degraded into its constituent parts and released back into the cell B. It is packaged in vesicles for transport outside the cell C. It is broken down into simpler compounds using hydrolytic enzymes D. It is excreted from the cell unchanged

FACTS: The cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins. QUESTION: What is the main component of the cell membrane? CHOICES: A. Carbohydrates B. Phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins C. DNA D. Fatty acids

FACTS: The cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins. QUESTION: What is unique about the structure of the cell membrane? CHOICES: A. It is a continuous layer of lipids B. It is made entirely of proteins C. It has three layers of phospholipids and water D. It has embedded proteins in a bilayer of phospholipids

FACTS: The cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins. QUESTION: What type of molecules are typically found "embedded" in the cell membrane? CHOICES: A. Fatty acids B. Carbohydrates C. Nucleic acids D. Proteins

FACTS: The cell membrane is selectively permeable. QUESTION: What is a key characteristic of the cell membrane? CHOICES: A. It allows all substances to pass through it freely. B. It regenerates itself continuously throughout the lifetime of the cell. C. It is selectively permeable, controlling what enters and leaves the cell. D. It is impervious to water and electrolytes.

FACTS: The cell membrane is selectively permeable. QUESTION: What role does selective permeability play in maintaining cellular function? CHOICES: A. It allows cells to grow and divide rapidly without limit. B. It enables cells to respond quickly to changes in their internal environment. C. It helps regulate the movement of nutrients, waste products, and ions across the cell membrane. D. It is a trait exclusive to plant cells.

FACTS: The cell membrane is selectively permeable. QUESTION: What would be the effect on cellular function if the cell membrane suddenly lost its selective permeability? CHOICES: A. The rate of cell growth and division would accelerate rapidly. B. The cell would experience no significant changes in metabolic activity. C. Cellular function would grind to a halt, leading to eventual cell death. D. The cell would become hyperactive and responsive only to external stimuli.

FACTS: Osmosis is the movement of water across a semipermeable membrane. QUESTION: What is osmosis? CHOICES: A. The movement of cells through tissues B. The process by which plants make food from sunlight C. The movement of water across a semipermeable membrane D. The breaking down of complex molecules into simpler ones

FACTS: Osmosis is the movement of water across a semipermeable membrane. QUESTION: Which type of structure does osmosis require to occur? CHOICES: A. A single cell wall B. A semipermeable membrane C. A rigid bone structure D. A fatty lipid bilayer

FACTS: Osmosis is the movement of water across a semipermeable membrane. QUESTION: Osmosis can cause what effect on a cell in certain situations? CHOICES: A. Increased size and volume B. Decreased growth rate C. Swelling due to water uptake D. Increased production of waste products

FACTS: Active transport moves molecules against their concentration gradient using ATP. QUESTION: What process is used by cells to move molecules against their concentration gradient using energy? CHOICES: A. Diffusion B. Osmosis C. Active transport D. Simple filtration

FACTS: Active transport moves molecules against their concentration gradient using ATP. QUESTION: Which of the following requirements must be met for active transport to occur in a cell? CHOICES: A. The molecule must have a high concentration on both sides of the membrane. B. The molecule must have a low concentration on one side of the membrane but a higher concentration on the other side C. No energy is required. D. The molecule cannot be large.

FACTS: Active transport moves molecules against their concentration gradient using ATP. QUESTION: What is used by cells to accomplish active transport? CHOICES: A. Osmosis B. Enzymatic catalysis C. Water D. ATP (adenosine triphosphate)

FACTS: Passive transport moves molecules down their concentration gradient without energy. QUESTION: What is a characteristic of passive transport? CHOICES: A. It always requires energy input from the cell. B. It moves molecules up their concentration gradient without energy. C. It moves molecules down their concentration gradient without energy. D. It only occurs in large cells.

FACTS: Passive transport moves molecules down their concentration gradient without energy. QUESTION: By what mechanism do cells move substances into or out of the cell according to need? CHOICES: A. Active transport B. Exocytosis C. Passive transport D. Endocytosis

FACTS: Passive transport moves molecules down their concentration gradient without energy. QUESTION: Which of the following substances would be moved through passive transport? CHOICES: A. A high concentration of salt being carried from one area to another with the help of ions. B. A low concentration of glucose being transported down its concentration gradient into a cell. C. A protein being pushed against its concentration gradient using mechanical means. D. An enzyme being secreted out of the cell through the cellular membrane.

FACTS: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells. QUESTION: What is produced as a result of mitosis? CHOICES: A. Two genetically identical haploid cells B. Four genetically different diploid cells C. One large, genetically identical cell D. Four genetically identical diploid cells

FACTS: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells. QUESTION: Which of the following statements describes a characteristic of mitosis? CHOICES: A. It is a type of cell division that results in four daughter cells. B. It is a type of sexual reproduction. C. It produces two cells with half the number of chromosomes. D. It produces genetically identical diploid cells.

FACTS: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells. QUESTION: What happens to the genetic material of the parent cell during mitosis? CHOICES: A. It is reduced by half B. It is multiplied four-fold C. The genetic material remains unchanged and copies itself D. It becomes completely altered through recombination

FACTS: Meiosis produces four genetically unique haploid cells. QUESTION: What is produced by meiosis? CHOICES: A. Two genetically identical diploid cells B. Four genetically unique haploid cells C. Eight genetically identical diploid cells D. One large cyst consisting of many cells

FACTS: Meiosis produces four genetically unique haploid cells. QUESTION: How do the daughter cells produced by meiosis differ from one another? CHOICES: A. They are all genetically identical B. They are all similar but with a few minor genetic variations C. They are each unique and genetically distinct from one another D. They all have the same number of chromosomes as their parent cell

FACTS: Meiosis produces four genetically unique haploid cells. QUESTION: What is special about the cells produced by the process of meiosis? CHOICES: A. Meiosis produces eight identical cells that are genetically 50% similar to the original cell B. Meiosis only occurs in eukaryotic organisms, never in prokaryotes C.
